faq: Can we use AI subscriptions we already have?
Where the provider allows it, through an API key or a supported account connection. Some plans cannot be used this way, and each provider sets its own limits. We check what applies before scoping.
Can it import our existing history?
From supported tools, or from exports you provide. It does not read an account’s history because someone signs in. What comes in, and who can see it, is agreed first.
What can agents actually do?
Research, check, draft, summarise and update records within the connections they are given. Actions that reach clients or other people, such as sending, wait for approval unless you decide otherwise.
Can the interface really change for our team?
Yes, on request. Someone describes a board, page or metric view, the workspace previews it, and a person with permission applies it. Your team keeps reshaping it after implementation.
Is it available now?
For teams, as a tailored implementation scoped in writing, with capabilities and connections agreed for your work. Me, the personal version, is in development.
How do permissions work across a team?
People sign in with their own accounts. Roles decide who reshapes the workspace, who approves, and what each person and agent can see. Private and shared context is set up during implementation.

about.title: Advice grounded in building.
bio: Amir advises leadership teams on where AI can create measurable value, how it should reshape workflows, and what people need to adopt it successfully. His work spans AI strategy, operating model design, implementation and capability building across travel, marketing, education, finance and clinical technology.

Amir has built AI systems for clients, from outbound growth engines to clinical trial management software, and launched two AI products of his own, grademy and pripitch. His team’s work won a Google hackathon.
why: Enamplify is a product and a practice. The workspace keeps a team’s context, accounts, tools and agents connected; the practice implements it around the way the team already works, and advises as that work changes.

The right starting point might be a focused build, a clearer plan or practical support for an existing team. We agree the scope, the responsibilities and how progress will be assessed before moving ahead.
about.markets: We work from London across the UK and Europe, and from Baku across Azerbaijan. The standard is the same in both: your data stays where you decide, and the capability stays with your people.

briefing.title: Structuring AI and agent work inside a company.
briefing.lede: Why individual chat accounts plateau, and how operations leaders organise shared context, specialist agent lanes, approval gates and adaptive workspaces so teams get reliable work out of AI.
briefing.meta: Unlisted executive briefing · 25 minutes · For COOs, Heads of Operations and transformation leads
briefing.gapTitle: Why most company AI rollouts stall at the chat box.
gapProse: Most organisations begin by handing out individual chat logins and running a short prompting workshop. People use the tool to rewrite emails or summarise isolated notes, while core operational work stays manual.

The bottleneck is rarely the model. It is the operating structure around the model. When an agent cannot see the current project brief, does not know which folder holds the approved template, tries to do five jobs in one prompt, or has no clear human review gate, teams stop trusting the output.

Getting real operational capacity from agents requires moving from isolated personal chats to a structured working environment where context, narrow responsibilities, permissions and review points are built into the workflow.
contrasts: Every person pastes fragments from memory; context is lost when the tab closes and nobody else can review the trail.
Projects, live calendars, approved folders and operating rules sit around the workspace so agents read current company truth.
A single prompt is asked to research, check numbers, draft copy and format the deliverable all at once.
Narrow roles handle source gathering, verification, drafting and formatting in parallel, then hand one draft to a named owner.
briefing.layersTitle: The four-layer structure for company agents.
briefing.layersDek: Treat agent capability as an operating design problem: what the workspace holds, how jobs are divided, where people approve, and how accounts are routed.

layers.name: Shared context and grounded sources
layers.what: Agents fail when they guess missing context. Before automating a task, gather the recurring inputs around a shared project space so every run starts from the same approved material.
points: Connect read-only project folders, calendars, briefs and reference documents to the workspace
Keep every generated line linked back to the source file or meeting note it came from
Separate approved company templates and style rules from ad-hoc personal notes

layers.name: Specialist agent lanes and handoffs
layers.role: Execution · How the work is divided
layers.what: Replace monolithic prompts with a small team of narrow specialists. Each lane has one clear input, one job and a visible status before the merged draft reaches a person.
points: Split recurring workflows into distinct lanes: source extraction, policy or data checking, drafting, and formatting
Run independent lanes in parallel so preparation finishes before the team review window
Require each lane to flag missing inputs or exceptions rather than inventing plausible filler

layers.name: Permission boundaries and approval gates
layers.role: Governance · What stays with a person
layers.what: Senior leaders need to defend how AI is used to a board, a client or a regulator. Make the boundary between autonomous preparation and human sign-off explicit inside the interface.
points: Allow scheduled or triggered runs to prepare drafts, boards and packs inside the workspace
Hold external actions, client communications and system updates behind a named human approver
Keep an auditable record of what sources were used, what was changed and who approved the output

layers.name: Account routing and retained sandboxes
layers.what: Operational workflows cannot stop because one provider account hits a usage cap or a browser tab closes mid-task. Route jobs deliberately and retain the working environment.
points: Match tasks to model accounts by complexity and data sensitivity, with automatic fallback when a limit is reached
Run browser research, code checks and file assembly inside a retained sandbox that can pause and resume
Adapt the visible workspace view (report shelf, kanban board, schedule or review table) to fit the job in front of the team

briefing.playbooksTitle: Three company workflows to structure first.
briefing.playbooksDek: Start where recurring preparation, checking and coordination consume skilled time every week.
playbooks: Trigger on the reporting calendar. One lane pulls campaign or operational metrics, a second checks commentary against the brief, and a third assembles the review pack for the account or operations lead to approve.

After a client or leadership call, extract agreed actions, match each item to an owner on the team board, and draft the proposal or follow-up note against the current project folder before anyone has to chase.
Embed standard operating procedures and acceptance criteria directly into the workspace view so new staff and reviewers check documents against grounded rules with every exception recorded.
briefing.wsIntro: Use this six-point diagnostic with your operations or functional leads to scope your first structured agent workflow before building.
checks: Which live calendars, folders, briefs and templates must sit inside the workspace so agents do not rely on pasted prompt memory?
How will we divide this workflow into narrow agent responsibilities (gathering, checking, drafting, formatting) instead of one general prompt?
Where does the prepared draft stop and wait for a named person? Which actions must never run without explicit sign-off?
Which model accounts and permissions apply to this data, and what is the fallback path when an account reaches its limit?
What view does the team actually need on screen to review this work quickly: a report shelf, a follow-up board, a delivery timeline or a checklist?
What observable change in preparation time, review quality and team follow-through will tell us this structure is working after 8 to 12 weeks?
briefing.closing: Choose one real workflow with clear inputs and a named owner. Prove the structure on live work before extending it across the wider organisation.
briefing.closeTitle: Want this structure built around your team?
briefing.closeBody: Tell us the workflow you want off your plate. We will scope a tailored Enamplify workspace, agent structure and support plan.

halves.lede: Software vendors hand you an empty login and leave your team to figure it out. Traditional consultancies hand you a slide deck and leave before anything runs. Enamplify is built and delivered as one unified practice.

items.label: Custom adaptive system
items.title: Engineered from scratch around how you operate.
items.sub: Adaptive from day one · Built for parallel scale
items.body: You never squeeze your business into someone else’s rigid software template. Your environment starts shaped around your workflows, terminology and permissions, and keeps reshaping through plain conversation.
points: Custom boards, exception ledgers, briefs and apps instead of fixed SaaS screens
A full team of specialist agents working in parallel across browser, code, files and systems
Continuous initiative on schedules and events, pausing cleanly at human approval gates
Your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or private model accounts, routed by task with fallback

items.label: Implementation consulting
items.title: Diagnosed, wired and scaled with our engineers.
items.body: You work directly with the engineers and operators building your system. We audit where skilled people lose their week, wire the integrations around real governance and stay embedded as it scales.
points: Operational diagnostic first: we map real bottlenecks, data boundaries and measurable outcomes
Hands-on wiring of your calendars, shared drives, CRMs, databases and sign-off rules
Live rollout with one or two core teams in weeks, tuned on real day-to-day work
Ongoing engineering and advisory stewardship as new teams and capabilities come online

contrasts: Gives everyone the same static template and leaves integration, adoption and workflow design to you.
Maps recommendations on paper without shipping a working system into daily operations.
Custom-builds your command system and agent team, wires it into your stack and scales it alongside your people.
